summary: Make a planet's local ring system occlude larger rings that pass through it, so a heliocentric orbit line stops at the edge of the local system and resumes past it instead of cutting across the pair's two concentric rings. Whole-disc erase, not a line hop — Max ruled it against a side-by-side preview 2026-08-18. Applies to every planet with moons, not just binaries. Requires OrbitConicField.js, whose parking-lot hold Max lifted the same day; the parking lot flags a real perf-architecture decision here, which is why this is scoped separately from the barycentre render. DESIGN PASS 2026-08-19 (13 agents, read-only): world-space ball keep-out tested against the circle point arcRoot already builds, packed into 8 new rows of the EXISTING DataTexture, predicate = same-local-system exemption + 3-D containment with NO radius comparison. Zero src/main.js edits. Plan + working-Claude's verification in implementation-plan.md.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Max's words: the larger orbit line does not cut into the binary planets' orbits. Where a heliocentric ring passes inside a planet's local system, it is not drawn — ONE clean gap the full width of the outermost local ring, not four nicks at the crossing points.

verifyVia.input: Park on wd-10 planet 3 with orbits visible, framed so both the pair's rings and the heliocentric ring are in shot; then sample the rendered image along the heliocentric ring's screen-space path.
verifyVia.observable: RULED 2026-08-19 (design pass §9.2): the endpoint criterion is a WORLD distance — the gap's two endpoints are the two points where the heliocentric ring's own circle crosses |P - C| = R, R being the local system's outermost ring radius. The screen measurement is CORROBORATION, and agrees only where the heliocentric ring and the local system are near-coplanar. Unit: over 360 theta samples of the heliocentric ring, the masked set is EXACTLY ONE contiguous run and both endpoints satisfy |P - C| = R to float tolerance. Live: the heliocentric ring has exactly one contiguous unlit span crossing the local system, no lit heliocentric pixels inside that radius, zero additional gaps.

acceptanceCriteria.resultNote: Live wd-10: exactly ONE masked run on planet 3's heliocentric circle at 400k samples; arc length 1.75627 vs chord 2R = 1.795735 (the 2% is the sampling step). Headless bisection lands both endpoints on |P-C| = R to 12 dp against sqrt(reff2).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: ⛔ THE TRAP, and it is fatal if missed: a local system's own rings must NOT be occluded by its own disc. The pair's inner ring (r1) lies ENTIRELY inside the outer ring (r2), so a naive 'mask anything inside the outermost local radius' rule erases the primary's ring completely — deleting the very thing the barycentre workstream shipped. The rule must exempt rings belonging to the same local system.

verifyVia.input: wd-10 planet 3, orbits visible, before and after the change; count the distinct rings drawn about the barycentre and measure their radii from the rendered image and from the live ring proxies.
verifyVia.observable: TWO rings still drawn about the empty point, at 5.53 and 19.55 primary radii — unchanged from the barycentre workstream's measurements. The inner ring is fully continuous, not partially or wholly erased. Reverting the same-system exemption must make THIS assertion go red specifically. ⛔ CORRECTED 2026-08-19: this assertion CANNOT go red at the parent commit — no occlusion exists there, so it passes trivially. Its falsification is a MUTATION: delete the same-system exemption line and readConic(r1Ring).keepOutCount goes 0 -> 1 and the ring is erased in full. Do not claim a parent-red this test cannot deliver.

acceptanceCriteria.resultNote: Live: the pair's rings still 0.254132 / 0.897868 (5.5332 / 19.5492 primary radii), both with keepOutCount 0. Falsified by MUTATION, not by parent — deleting the exemption masks r1 at all 360 sampled angles.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every planet with moons gets the keep-out, not just the 27 that earned barycentric rings. Max's standing preference for the general answer over a special case, same as his no-mass-ratio-cutoff ruling on the wobble.

verifyVia.input: Enumerate the keep-out discs the renderer registers for a system with a mix of dominated and undominated planets — wd-10 (planets 1, 2, 3 dominated; planet 4 has three moons and is not).
verifyVia.observable: A keep-out disc exists for EVERY planet carrying at least one moon, including planet 4, and none exists for planet 0, which has none. The disc radius equals that planet's outermost local ring radius in every case.

acceptanceCriteria.resultNote: Live: 4 discs for 4 moon-bearing planets, none for planet 0. Ring 6 is planet 4 — UNDOMINATED, 3 moons — with reff2 = 90.453102 = 9.5107^2, its outermost local ring. No special case for the 27 pairs.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A masked pixel is still a clickable ring. Occlusion changes what is DRAWN, never what is selectable — otherwise the star-orbit line becomes unclickable across a span the user can see it ought to occupy.

verifyVia.input: Click the heliocentric orbit line at a point inside the occluded span, and at a point outside it, on wd-10 planet 3.
verifyVia.observable: Both clicks select the same planet's orbit. hitTestOrbits reads the baked perimeter attribute (OrbitLine.js:57-65) and that attribute is untouched by this change.

acceptanceCriteria.resultNote: Unit fence green and live state intact: 16/16 ring proxies visible with intact baked hit perimeters, and the disc path provably touches neither. ⛔ The live CLICK inside the occluded span is UNRUN.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: No ring is added or removed, and the perf-architecture decision the parking lot flagged is made explicitly rather than by accident. CONIC_MAX stays 64 and the descriptor count is unchanged — the keep-out list is a SEPARATE, much shorter list (one entry per moon-bearing planet, worst case 8 in FENCE-221) and must not consume ring descriptor slots.

verifyVia.input: Count descriptors before and after on the worst measured system; then a like-for-like frame-time comparison on the same seed, same camera pose, same window size, parent commit vs build commit.
verifyVia.observable: Descriptor count identical before and after on the same system (16 on wd-10, measured live 2026-08-19). CONIC_MAX stays 64. ⛔ CORRECTED 2026-08-19: (a) 'worst system stays at 27 of 64 — measured by tools/barycentre-probe.mjs' — the probe does NOT print a per-system descriptor total; its 27 is the companion-pair count across FENCE-221. (b) 'worst case 8 in FENCE-221' — 8 is SOL's moon-bearing-planet count, not FENCE-221's. KEEPOUT_MAX = 8 is justified from the PLANET ceiling (StarSystemGenerator.js:80-81 planetRange upper bound 8, clamped at :499; the one path that can exceed it is :502 Math.max(rolledPlanetCount, knownSorted.length), whose only shipped instance is Sol at 8 moon-bearing planets), NOT from any ring count. Frame time is stated as a MEASURED number with sample size — same seed, frozen pose, same window, parent commit vs build commit, PAGE RELOADED BETWEEN ARMS, N >= 300 frames per arm, median + p95. If the shader gains a per-pixel loop, its bound is a declared constant sized and justified in a comment the way CONIC_MAX is.

acceptanceCriteria.resultNote: Descriptor count 16 before and after; CONIC_MAX 64; texture 64x18; KEEPOUT_MAX = 8 declared and justified; shader loop bound is that literal. ⛔ The MEASURED frame-time number the AC demands is NOT taken — no headless harness in this repo can produce one. AC is not satisfied until a live parent-vs-build comparison runs.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Only rings that genuinely pass INSIDE a local system are occluded by it. A moon ring belonging to a neighbouring planet, or a binary-STAR orbit ring, must not silently vanish because it grazes some other planet's disc in SCREEN space. ⛔ CORRECTED 2026-08-19: the original clause also named an asteroid-belt ring, which cannot exist — updateFromSystem reads only starOrbitLines (:524), orbitLines (:526) and planets[i].moonOrbitLines (:531); system.asteroidBelts (main.js:7841) is not among them and no `new OrbitLine(` site is a belt.

verifyVia.input: On a binary-star system with several moon-bearing planets (wd-10 qualifies: isBinary true, 2 star-orbit rings, 5 planet rings, 4 moon-bearing planets), enumerate every ring proxy drawn before and after.
verifyVia.observable: ⛔ CORRECTED 2026-08-19: the original observable — 'the same 16 rings are present after' — passes TRIVIALLY with or without the feature, because the descriptor list is untouched by any shader-side mask. It is a fence, not a test of the predicate. The real test is per-ring: readConic(i).keepOutCount === 0 for BOTH binary-star rings and for every neighbouring planet's moon ring, and === 1 for the moon-bearing planet's own heliocentric ring. MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-19 on wd-10 before any code: of 14 foreign rings exactly 1 is masked (planet 3's own heliocentric ring, gap^2 = 0); the nearest false positive misses by gap^2 = 2,427,689 against Reff^2 = 0.806, a margin of ~3e6. Fence, retained: all 16 ring proxies still present.

acceptanceCriteria.resultNote: Live: both binary-STAR rings at keepOutCount 0; every moon ring at 0; planet 0's heliocentric ring at 0. All 16 ring proxies still present and visible. Nearest false positive misses by gap^2 = 2,427,689 against Reff^2 = 0.806.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Max's gate: does the star-orbit line now read as passing BEHIND a solid local system, rather than as a broken or missing line? And across an ordinary moon system — not just the pair — does the new gap look deliberate or does it look like a rendering fault?

verifyVia.input: Max looks at wd-10 planet 3 (the pair) and at an ordinary multi-moon planet with orbits visible, live or on a recording.
verifyVia.observable: Max says it reads as solid. Never PASSed by an agent — deferred-to-max.

acceptanceCriteria.resultNote: Max's gate alone. Never passed by an agent.

inputs: src/objects/OrbitConicField.js — the ONLY source of ring pixels. src/objects/OrbitRingSDF.js:49 'This class no longer renders anything'; ring meshes carry empty geometry on layer 10 and exist as transform proxies plus a parameter bag.

OrbitConicField.updateFromSystem reads exactly three hardcoded property names — :524 system.starOrbitLines, :526 system.orbitLines, :531 planets[i].moonOrbitLines — and appends them in that order, so ring provenance (which planet a ring belongs to) is known at append time and is where the same-system exemption must be recorded.

The per-ring RGBA32F DataTexture (CONIC_MAX wide x CONIC_TEX_ROWS tall, read with texelFetch) and the GLSL loop bound at OrbitConicField.js:251 — a keep-out list needs its own channel, not a stolen ring slot.
entry.moonOrbitLines and the _baryCentred flag from binary-barycentre-render-2026-08-18 — the local system's centre is the bary ring centre where one exists, and the planet mesh otherwise.
docs/PARKING_LOT.md:230-241 (follow-up list :230-237, sequencing note :239-241) — the deferral Max lifted, and the perf-architecture note that made this a scoped workstream rather than a patch.
outputs: Rendered ring pixels only. No ring object, radius, centre, transform, visibility flag or hit-test attribute changes.
A keep-out list consumed by the conic field's fullscreen pass.
mustStayWorking: ⛔ The pair's inner ring. It lies entirely inside the outer ring, so the same-system exemption is load-bearing, not a nicety — without it this workstream silently deletes what binary-barycentre-render-2026-08-18 shipped. AC-LOCAL-RINGS-SURVIVE exists solely to catch that.

The angular-size fade (OrbitConicField.js:75-79 + :107 + :121-129 (JS mirror) + :174-177 (GLSL) + :344 (the multiply)), which is the shipped mechanism for dropping sub-pixel rings. Occlusion must compose with it, not replace or double-count it.
The camera-proximity fade stays RETIRED per Max's UAT ruling 2026-08-01 (OrbitConicField.js:503-504). Do not revive it as a way to implement this.
hitTestOrbits and hover: main.js prefers the baked perimeter attribute (OrbitLine.js:57-65, main.js:7013), and the material.opacity shim that hover reads and restores.
CONIC_MAX stays 64 and OrbitConicField's GLSL loop bound is not raised — :251 is a shader loop bound, so changing it recompiles, and :396/:406/:635 all size off it.
The 27 barycentric ring pairs and the planet-following branch from the previous workstream both keep rendering exactly as measured in that workstream's live-integration-evidence.md.
